name: Proofreader API
plain: Checks spelling and grammar on the device.
meaning: Local proofreading of what the person typed.

access.iframe: Same as top level; cross-origin iframes need a permissions policy where listed

data.metric: Checks spelling and grammar on the device.

limits.headline: Can check spelling and grammar of text you typed, on your device, in Chrome testing
limits.user_action: You type in a form or comment box on a site in the Chrome trial
can: Suggest fixes for text you typed
Keep your text on your device
cannot: Work for normal visitors yet, since it is a developer or origin trial
Work in Edge, Firefox, Safari or on phones
Check text you have not typed or pasted into the page
Send your text to a server for this feature
limits.differs: Only in a Chrome testing trial today. Not in Firefox, Safari or on phones.

story.what_it_is: A page can check spelling and grammar for you using an AI model on your device.

marketing.name: Built-in AI
marketing.pitch: Chrome's built in AI includes writing helpers that run on the device, so text stays private.

story.for_you: You type and see corrections, like red underlines. The checking happens on your computer, so your draft is not sent out. Not every site can use it yet.
story.for_makers: Makers get grammar help with no external service or extra cost. It keeps private drafts private. It is still in testing, so it is not available to all users.

use_cases.example: A web email app checks tone and typos on device before you press send.
A homework site flags grammar mistakes in a student's essay, without storing the essay.
A post box on a web social site marks typos as you write.
A web document editor fixes grammar offline on a plane.
A seller tool on a marketplace checks product descriptions for errors.
A page helps a reader with dyslexia fix spelling as they type.
A company wiki checks for mistakes in internal pages with no cloud call.

history.change: Trial in 2026; status varies in docs
